extracted.intended_audience: administrators and legal/policy staff of educational institutions (Title IX Coordinators), state education officials, attorneys, and advocacy organizations implementing or responding to Title IX §106.44
extracted.subtask_description: Explanation of recipients' obligations under final Title IX §106.44: when a recipient has knowledge of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination, what employee reporting duties trigger the duty to respond, required monitoring for barriers to reporting, and the specific types of actions recipients must take to end, prevent, and remedy sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond promptly and effectively when recipient has knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.44(a)(1): a recipient with knowledge of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination in its education program or activity must respond promptly and effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This duty is triggered when the recipient has 'knowledge' (see separate knowledge standard entries). The Department clarified that this obligation is not a standard of strict liability and does not require action for conduct that occurred before any employee became aware. See discussion of timing, scope, and that responses must be 'prompt and effective' (further explained in §106.44(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with §106.44(b)-(k) (specific required actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.44(a)(2): a recipient must comply with the other paragraphs of §106.44 to address sex discrimination in its education program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department revised §106.44(a)(2) to clarify recipients must take the actions outlined in §106.44(b)-(k), providing specific instruction rather than an open-ended obligation. These paragraphs set out duties such as monitoring for barriers, notification duties, supportive/remedial measures, emergency removal procedures, informal resolution options, and grievance safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expanded knowledge standard: knowledge when any non-confidential employee has information
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department expanded the knowledge standard so a recipient is deemed to have knowledge of sex-based discrimination when any non-confidential employee has information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For elementary and secondary recipients, all non-confidential employees must notify the Title IX Coordinator when they have such information. For other recipients, employees with responsibility for administrative leadership, teaching, or advising must notify. Other non-confidential employees must either notify the Title IX Coordinator or provide the Title IX Coordinator's contact information and complaint procedures. This replaces the narrower 2020 'actual knowledge' definition that limited notice in postsecondary settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-confidential employees' reporting duties (§106.44(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-confidential employees who receive information that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination must take specified actions: notify the Title IX Coordinator or provide contact information and complaint instructions to the reporting person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title IX Coordinators and any contractor delegated Title IX responsibilities who have information must respond consistent with the regulations. The nature of the employee's role determines which of the notification options apply (see §106.44(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond when conduct 'reasonably may' constitute sex discrimination (low threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient need not have incontrovertible proof that conduct violates Title IX; if the conduct reasonably may be sex discrimination, the recipient must respond in accordance with §106.44.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department cites prior interpretations and case law to confirm that an objective allegation sufficient to 'reasonably' indicate sexual harassment or sex discrimination triggers the duty to respond (e.g., Doe v. Fairfax Cnty. Sch. Bd.; Davis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of 'actual knowledge' and 'deliberate indifference' standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations remove the 2020 'actual knowledge' and 'deliberate indifference' standards for administrative enforcement and instead define clear steps recipients must take under §106.44.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department concluded the deliberate indifference standard was inappropriate in the administrative enforcement context because it limited required responses and created gaps where sex discrimination could go unaddressed. The new approach sets uniform, more robust expectations across forms of sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring for barriers to reporting (§106.44(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.44(b) requires recipients to monitor for and address barriers that prevent or deter individuals from reporting possible sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Barriers include inaccessible reporting processes, confusing grievance procedures, unreachable Title IX staff, discouraging staff, lengthy response times, and fears of being disbelieved or retaliated against. Recipients must take steps reasonably calculated to address identified barriers (tailored responses). Examples: targeted trainings, publication of Title IX contact info, relocating Title IX office to a visible location, adequate staffing, and user-friendly materials. Climate surveys are permitted but not mandated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailored, reasonably-calculated responses to identified barriers
rubrics_metrics.description: When a recipient becomes aware of a barrier to reporting, it must take steps that are reasonably calculated to address that barrier and tailor its response to the specific impediments identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declines to prescribe specific mandatory actions or require particular measures (e.g., mandatory follow-up with reporters), allowing recipients to choose strategies appropriate to their environment. However, responses should be fact-specific and may include a range of measures described in §106.44(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients not strictly liable; obligations tied to knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations are not intended to impose strict liability for all sex discrimination; a recipient's duty to respond arises only when it has knowledge of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department amended the language to emphasize 'with knowledge' to address concerns that the earlier proposal appeared to create strict liability. If no employee (including Title IX Coordinator or delegated contractor) has knowledge, the recipient cannot be expected to respond promptly and effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator must monitor for and address barriers even before receiving reports
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must require its Title IX Coordinator to monitor for and address barriers to reporting under §106.44(b), regardless of whether the Coordinator has received information about specific conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This proactive monitoring duty requires institutional steps (training, outreach, structural changes) to reduce impediments to reporting and access to remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical limitations when only respondent-employee has knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: If the only employee of a recipient with information about possible sex discrimination is the alleged perpetrator, the recipient is not relieved of obligations but may be practically unable to respond until another non-confidential employee becomes aware.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department recognizes practical constraints but clarifies the legal duty remains; recipients should still take appropriate steps when knowledge exists or becomes available to others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform standards across types of sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.44 broadly covers all forms of sex discrimination and the Department determined standards should be uniform rather than singling out sexual harassment with a different (deliberate indifference) standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department found singling out sexual harassment raised equity and rationality concerns and could erode institutional trust; the final regulations apply consistent obligations across prohibited sex-based harassment and discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactions with Section 504 and the IDEA; emergency removal safeguards (§106.44(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in §106.44 authorizes measures that conflict with Section 504 or the IDEA; emergency removal provisions require an individualized safety and risk analysis and provide notice and immediate opportunity to challenge removal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must ensure emergency removals are consistent with IDEA/Section 504/ADA protections and follow §106.44(h)'s procedural safeguards; the regulations do not modify other federal civil rights rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutrality and impartiality of Title IX Coordinator preserved
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations do not eliminate neutrality or impartiality from the Title IX Coordinator role; recipients are not acting as prosecutors but must ensure fair, unbiased treatment of parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protections and safeguards (training requirements, conflict-of-interest rules, grievance procedure provisions, informal resolution safeguards, appeals) are included in the regulations to promote impartiality and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual enrollment obligations: each recipient liable for its own program participants
rubrics_metrics.description: When students are enrolled in two recipient institutions simultaneously (dual enrollment), each recipient has independent obligations under Title IX to protect participants from sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neither institution should assume the other is solely responsible; effective supportive/remedial measures may implicate both institutions and both should act as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of climate surveys and reporting tools permitted but not required
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may use campus surveys (climate surveys) to monitor barriers to reporting and increase awareness, but the Department declines to mandate specific tools or surveys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some States and VAWA 2022 require climate surveys; these regulations allow but do not require their use. The Department emphasizes flexibility in choosing monitoring tools appropriate to the recipient's environment.
